/-!
# Birkhoff conjecture

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex billiard table, i.e. a bounded domain whose
boundary $\partial\Omega$ is a $C^2$ closed curve with strictly positive curvature. A billiard ball
moves in straight lines inside $\Omega$ and reflects elastically at $\partial\Omega$ (angle of
incidence equals angle of reflection). The *billiard map* $T$ acts on the phase space
$\partial\Omega \times (0, \pi)$, whose points are pairs (position on the boundary, angle between
the outgoing direction and the positively oriented tangent). The billiard is *integrable* if a
neighbourhood of the boundary $\partial\Omega \times \{0, \pi\}$ of the phase space is foliated by
homotopically non-trivial invariant curves of $T$. (Equivalently, a neighbourhood of
$\partial\Omega$ inside $\Omega$ is foliated by convex caustics.)

**Birkhoff conjecture.** If a billiard table is strictly convex and integrable, is its boundary
necessarily an ellipse? The conjectured answer is yes; ellipses (including circles) are integrable.

Note that the whole phase space is foliated by invariant curves only for disks: this is a
theorem of Bialy (1993), so the conjecture concerns integrability near the boundary.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [Wikipedia, Dynamical billiards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_billiards)
- V. Kaloshin, A. Sorrentino, *On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards*,
  Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), [arXiv:1612.09194](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09194)
- M. Bialy, *Convex billiards and a theorem by E. Hopf*, Math. Z. 214 (1993), 147–154
-/

blocks.docstring:
A *strictly convex billiard table* is described by its boundary curve `γ`: a $C^2$ simple closed
curve in the plane, parametrised with period `1` and traversed counterclockwise, whose curvature
is everywhere strictly positive. The last condition is expressed as the positivity of the area
form $\gamma' \wedge \gamma''$; in particular it forces `γ` to be regular ($\gamma' \neq 0$).

def BilliardRel (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (p q : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  p.2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π ∧ q.2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π ∧
    (∃ r > 0, γ q.1 = γ p.1 + r • direction γ p.1 p.2) ∧
    direction γ q.1 q.2 = (ℝ ∙ unitTangent γ q.1).reflection (direction γ p.1 p.2)
blocks.docstring:
The billiard map of the table bounded by `γ`, as a relation on the phase space
$\mathbb{R} \times (0, \pi)$ (position parameter, angle with the tangent; the position is only
relevant modulo the period `1`). `BilliardRel γ (s, θ) (s', θ')` holds when the ball leaving
`γ s` in the direction `direction γ s θ` next hits the boundary at `γ s'`, and the direction
`direction γ s' θ'` in which it leaves `γ s'` is the mirror image of its incoming direction in
the tangent line at `γ s'` (law of reflection). For a strictly convex curve this relation is the
graph of the billiard map.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Submodule.reflection (used for the reflection law); no billiard/geodesic-flow notions exist.
justification.name: Birkhoff.BilliardRel
justification.why_needed: The billiard map (next hit point + law of reflection) is absent from Mathlib; given as a relation, which is the graph of the billiard map under the strict convexity hypotheses.

structure IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  continuous : Continuous f
  periodic : Function.Periodic f 1
  mem_Ioo : ∀ s, f s ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π
  forward_invariant : ∀ s q, BilliardRel γ (s, f s) q → q.2 = f q.1
  backward_invariant : ∀ p s, BilliardRel γ p (s, f s) → p.2 = f p.1
blocks.docstring:
A (homotopically non-trivial) *invariant curve* of the billiard map of the table bounded by `γ`,
written as the graph of a continuous function `f` from the boundary (parametrised with period `1`)
to the angles `(0, π)`. Invariance means that the billiard map sends the graph of `f` onto itself.
By Birkhoff's theorem on twist maps, every homotopically non-trivial closed invariant curve of the
billiard map is such a graph.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Function.IsFixedPt / MapsTo of a set under a function (billiard map is only available as a relation here).
justification.name: Birkhoff.IsInvariantCurve
justification.why_needed: Homotopically non-trivial invariant curve of the billiard map (as an invariant continuous periodic graph over the boundary).

blocks.name: IsInvariantCurve
blocks.text:
/--
A (homotopically non-trivial) *invariant curve* of the billiard map of the table bounded by `γ`,
written as the graph of a continuous function `f` from the boundary (parametrised with period `1`)
to the angles `(0, π)`. Invariance means that the billiard map sends the graph of `f` onto itself.
By Birkhoff's theorem on twist maps, every homotopically non-trivial closed invariant curve of the
billiard map is such a graph.
-/
structure IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  continuous : Continuous f
  periodic : Function.Periodic f 1
  mem_Ioo : ∀ s, f s ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π
  forward_invariant : ∀ s q, BilliardRel γ (s, f s) q → q.2 = f q.1
  backward_invariant : ∀ p s, BilliardRel γ p (s, f s) → p.2 = f p.1

def IsIntegrable (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : Set (ℝ → ℝ), (∀ f ∈ F, IsInvariantCurve γ f) ∧
    F.Pairwise (fun f g => ∀ s, f s ≠ g s) ∧
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ s, ∀ θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ε ∪ Set.Ioo (π - ε) π, ∃ f ∈ F, f s = θ
blocks.docstring:
The billiard in the table bounded by `γ` is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary
`{θ = 0} ∪ {θ = π}` of the phase space is foliated by invariant curves: there is a family `F`
of invariant curves with pairwise disjoint graphs whose union contains
$\mathbb{R} \times ((0, \varepsilon) \cup (\pi - \varepsilon, \pi))$ for some
$\varepsilon > 0$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MeasureTheory.Integrable (unrelated meaning); no foliation/caustic notions in Mathlib.
justification.name: Birkhoff.IsIntegrable
justification.why_needed: Birkhoff-integrability of a billiard: a neighbourhood of the boundary of phase space foliated by invariant curves. Not in Mathlib.

blocks.name: IsIntegrable
blocks.text:
/--
The billiard in the table bounded by `γ` is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary
`{θ = 0} ∪ {θ = π}` of the phase space is foliated by invariant curves: there is a family `F`
of invariant curves with pairwise disjoint graphs whose union contains
$\mathbb{R} \times ((0, \varepsilon) \cup (\pi - \varepsilon, \pi))$ for some
$\varepsilon > 0$.
-/
def IsIntegrable (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : Set (ℝ → ℝ), (∀ f ∈ F, IsInvariantCurve γ f) ∧
    F.Pairwise (fun f g => ∀ s, f s ≠ g s) ∧
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ s, ∀ θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ε ∪ Set.Ioo (π - ε) π, ∃ f ∈ F, f s = θ

def IsEllipse (S : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : ℝ² ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ², S = e '' Metric.sphere 0 1
blocks.docstring:
A subset of the plane is an *ellipse* if it is the image of the unit circle under an affine
automorphism of the plane. Circles are ellipses.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question whose conjectured answer is 'yes' (every strictly convex integrable planar billiard has elliptic boundary, circles included); the main formalization subtlety is fixing the meaning of 'integrable' (standard: a neighbourhood of the boundary of the phase cylinder is foliated by invariant curves / the table admits a neighbourhood of the boundary foliated by convex caustics — whole-phase-space foliation is Bialy's already-proved theorem) and of 'strictly convex' (smooth, e.g. C^2, closed curve with strictly positive curvature), with the ambient space implicitly the Euclidean plane.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 states the conjecture as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ, IsStrictlyConvexCurve γ → IsIntegrable γ → IsEllipse (range γ)` with: table = C² 1-periodic simple closed curve with positive curvature (areaForm(γ',γ'')>0, which also forces regularity and fixes orientation); billiard map as the relation on (s,θ) ∈ ℝ×(0,π) given by ray-hitting plus `Submodule.reflection` in the tangent line (unit vectors, so θ' is determined); invariant curves = continuous 1-periodic graphs f:ℝ→(0,π) with T(graph)=graph (forward+backward invariance); integrability = a family of pairwise-disjoint invariant graphs covering ℝ×((0,ε)∪(π−ε,π)) — a genuine neighbourhood of the phase-cylinder boundary, not Bialy's whole-cylinder case; ellipse = affine-automorphism image of the unit circle (includes circles, excludes degenerate ones). Orientation consistency checked in Mathlib: ω x (rotation θ x) = ‖x‖² sin θ > 0 for θ∈(0,π), matching the curvature sign convention. Ellipses satisfy the hypothesis (confocal caustics), so it is not vacuous. Edits: removed an unproven parenthetical remark from a docstring, fixed the module docstring (one-vs-two boundary components) and dropped an arXiv reference I could not verify; reflowed one line.

context: George David Birkhoff (March 21, 1884 – November 12, 1944) was an American mathematician. He is considered one of the top American mathematicians of his generation. He made valuable contributions to the theory of differential equations, dynamical systems, the four-color problem, the three-body problem, and general relativity. Today, Birkhoff is best remembered for the ergodic theorem. The George D. Birkhoff House, his residence in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been designated a National Historic Landmark.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single slot matches the statement. The notes' guidance (local integrability near the phase-space boundary rather than Bialy's global version; strict convexity as positive curvature with C² regularity; Euclidean plane) was followed.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Birkhoff conjecture

Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a strictly convex billiard table, i.e. a bounded domain whose
boundary $\partial\Omega$ is a $C^2$ closed curve with strictly positive curvature. A billiard ball
moves in straight lines inside $\Omega$ and reflects elastically at $\partial\Omega$ (angle of

homotopically non-trivial invariant curves of $T$. (Equivalently, a neighbourhood of
$\partial\Omega$ inside $\Omega$ is foliated by convex caustics.)

**Birkhoff conjecture.** If a billiard table is strictly convex and integrable, is its boundary
necessarily an ellipse? The conjectured answer is yes; ellipses (including circles) are integrable.

Note that the whole phase space is foliated by invariant curves only for disks: this is a
theorem of Bialy (1993), so the conjecture concerns integrability near the boundary.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, George David Birkhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_David_Birkhoff)
- [Wikipedia, Dynamical billiards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamical_billiards)
- V. Kaloshin, A. Sorrentino, *On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards*,
  Ann. of Math. 188 (2018), [arXiv:1612.09194](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.09194)
- M. Bialy, *Convex billiards and a theorem by E. Hopf*, Math. Z. 214 (1993), 147–154
-/

open Real
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace Birkhoff

/--
A *strictly convex billiard table* is described by its boundary curve `γ`: a $C^2$ simple closed
curve in the plane, parametrised with period `1` and traversed counterclockwise, whose curvature
is everywhere strictly positive. The last condition is expressed as the positivity of the area
form $\gamma' \wedge \gamma''$; in particular it forces `γ` to be regular ($\gamma' \neq 0$).
-/
structure IsStrictlyConvexCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  curvature_pos : ∀ s, 0 < positiveOrientation.areaForm (deriv γ s) (iteratedDeriv 2 γ s)

/-- The unit tangent vector of the curve `γ` at the parameter `s`. -/
noncomputable def unitTangent (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (s : ℝ) : ℝ² :=
  ‖deriv γ s‖⁻¹ • deriv γ s

/--
The direction of the billiard ball leaving the boundary point `γ s` at angle `θ` with the
positively oriented tangent: the unit tangent rotated counterclockwise by `θ`. For a
counterclockwise curve and `θ ∈ (0, π)` this direction points into the table.
-/
noncomputable def direction (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (s θ : ℝ) : ℝ² :=
  positiveOrientation.rotation (θ : Real.Angle) (unitTangent γ s)

/-- The direction of a phase point is a unit vector (at a regular parameter of the curve). -/
@[category API, AMS 37]
theorem norm_direction {γ : ℝ → ℝ²} {s : ℝ} (hs : deriv γ s ≠ 0) (θ : ℝ) :
    ‖direction γ s θ‖ = 1 := by
  rw [direction, LinearIsometryEquiv.norm_map, unitTangent, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hs)]

/--
The billiard map of the table bounded by `γ`, as a relation on the phase space
$\mathbb{R} \times (0, \pi)$ (position parameter, angle with the tangent; the position is only
relevant modulo the period `1`). `BilliardRel γ (s, θ) (s', θ')` holds when the ball leaving
`γ s` in the direction `direction γ s θ` next hits the boundary at `γ s'`, and the direction
`direction γ s' θ'` in which it leaves `γ s'` is the mirror image of its incoming direction in
the tangent line at `γ s'` (law of reflection). For a strictly convex curve this relation is the
graph of the billiard map.
-/
def BilliardRel (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (p q : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  p.2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π ∧ q.2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π ∧
    (∃ r > 0, γ q.1 = γ p.1 + r • direction γ p.1 p.2) ∧
    direction γ q.1 q.2 = (ℝ ∙ unitTangent γ q.1).reflection (direction γ p.1 p.2)

/--
A (homotopically non-trivial) *invariant curve* of the billiard map of the table bounded by `γ`,
written as the graph of a continuous function `f` from the boundary (parametrised with period `1`)
to the angles `(0, π)`. Invariance means that the billiard map sends the graph of `f` onto itself.
By Birkhoff's theorem on twist maps, every homotopically non-trivial closed invariant curve of the
billiard map is such a graph.
-/
structure IsInvariantCurve (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop where
  continuous : Continuous f
  periodic : Function.Periodic f 1
  mem_Ioo : ∀ s, f s ∈ Set.Ioo 0 π
  forward_invariant : ∀ s q, BilliardRel γ (s, f s) q → q.2 = f q.1
  backward_invariant : ∀ p s, BilliardRel γ p (s, f s) → p.2 = f p.1

/--
The billiard in the table bounded by `γ` is *integrable* if a neighbourhood of the boundary
`{θ = 0} ∪ {θ = π}` of the phase space is foliated by invariant curves: there is a family `F`
of invariant curves with pairwise disjoint graphs whose union contains
$\mathbb{R} \times ((0, \varepsilon) \cup (\pi - \varepsilon, \pi))$ for some
$\varepsilon > 0$.
-/
def IsIntegrable (γ : ℝ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : Set (ℝ → ℝ), (∀ f ∈ F, IsInvariantCurve γ f) ∧
    F.Pairwise (fun f g => ∀ s, f s ≠ g s) ∧
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ s, ∀ θ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 ε ∪ Set.Ioo (π - ε) π, ∃ f ∈ F, f s = θ

/-- A subset of the plane is an *ellipse* if it is the image of the unit circle under an affine
automorphism of the plane. Circles are ellipses. -/
def IsEllipse (S : Set ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : ℝ² ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ², S = e '' Metric.sphere 0 1

/-- The unit circle is an ellipse. -/
@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem isEllipse_sphere : IsEllipse (Metric.sphere 0 1) :=
  ⟨AffineEquiv.refl ℝ ℝ², by simp⟩

/--
**Birkhoff conjecture.**
If a billiard table is strictly convex and integrable, is its boundary necessarily an ellipse?

Here a strictly convex table has a $C^2$ boundary with strictly positive curvature, and
integrability means that a neighbourhood of the boundary of the phase space is foliated by
invariant curves of the billiard map. The conjectured answer is yes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 37 52]
theorem birkhoff :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ γ : ℝ → ℝ², IsStrictlyConvexCurve γ → IsIntegrable γ →
      IsEllipse (Set.range γ) := by
  sorry

end Birkhoff

items: Ambient space: the Euclidean plane ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), with the repo's positive orientation instance (verified: areaForm e₀ e₁ = 1 and rightAngleRotation e₀ = e₁, so positive area form = counterclockwise and J = left/inward normal).

'Strictly convex billiard table' is encoded by its boundary curve γ : ℝ → ℝ²: C² (`ContDiff ℝ 2 γ`), 1-periodic, injective on [0,1) (simple closed), with everywhere strictly positive curvature `0 < areaForm (γ') (γ'')` (this also forces regularity γ' ≠ 0 and counterclockwise orientation). This follows the decomposition note ('smooth, e.g. C², closed curve with strictly positive curvature'); note the standard literature (Kaloshin–Sorrentino) often takes C^r with r ≥ 3 as a standing assumption — a reviewer may prefer a higher regularity class. Positive curvature (rather than mere geometric strict convexity) was chosen because it is the standard hypothesis making the billiard map a C¹ twist map; it makes the conjecture weaker/safer than a no-flat-segments reading.

Phase space is ℝ × (0,π) (boundary parameter modulo the period 1, angle θ between the outgoing direction and the positively oriented tangent). The billiard map is given as a relation `BilliardRel`: the ray from γ s in direction rotation_θ(unit tangent) hits the curve at γ s' (∃ r > 0, γ s' = γ s + r • v), and the outgoing direction at s' is the reflection of the incoming direction in the tangent line (`Submodule.reflection (ℝ ∙ unitTangent γ s')`), with θ' ∈ (0,π). For strictly convex curves this is exactly the graph of the billiard map (unique second intersection, transversal chord). Checked on the unit circle: gives (s,θ) ↦ (s + θ/π, θ).

Invariant curves: homotopically non-trivial invariant curves are encoded as graphs of continuous 1-periodic functions f : ℝ → (0,π) with T(graph f) = graph f, encoded as forward invariance plus backward invariance (T⁻¹(graph) ⊆ graph). Using graphs relies on Birkhoff's theorem that essential invariant curves of twist maps are (Lipschitz) graphs; this is the standard way integrability is phrased.

'Integrable' = local integrability in the standard sense: a neighbourhood of the boundary of the phase cylinder is foliated by invariant curves, encoded as a family F of invariant curves with pairwise disjoint graphs whose union contains ℝ × ((0,ε) ∪ (π−ε, π)) for some ε > 0. Both boundary components are included for a literal reading (by reversibility of the billiard map, one component would be equivalent). 'Foliated' is read as 'partitioned into' (disjoint leaves); no extra continuity of the leaf family is imposed. Whole-phase-space foliation (Bialy's theorem) is deliberately NOT required.
'Ellipse' = image of the unit circle Metric.sphere 0 1 under an affine automorphism ℝ² ≃ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ² (includes circles).
Yes/no question formalized as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ...`, with `answer(True)` meaning the conjectured positive answer (boundary necessarily an ellipse).

reviewer_notes: Source is a one-line list entry; 'integrable' fixed as the standard local meaning (neighbourhood of ∂(phase cylinder) foliated by invariant curves) and 'strictly convex' as C² closed curve with strictly positive curvature, per the decomposition notes; invariant curves are taken to be graphs (Birkhoff's theorem for twist maps), the standard convention. Regularity C² follows the notes and Bialy/Bialy–Mironov; a reviewer might prefer C^∞. c02, c03, c05 are also faithful (equivalent formulations: (p,v)-coordinates with compact graphs; (s,θ) with unnormalized directions; oriented-chord coordinates with one boundary component + IsOpen) — c04 was chosen as the cleanest. Rejected: c01 requires the union of caustic frontiers to EQUAL the metric δ-collar {infDist x ∂K < δ}, which fails even for non-circular ellipses (confocal caustics are not parallel curves), so its hypothesis is not the intended one; c06, c07, c08 require the foliated region to be exactly a constant-width collar {0 < s₁−s₀ < ε} in the chosen parametrization, which forces the chord curve {s₁ = s₀+ε} to be an invariant curve — an extra parametrization-dependent restriction that is not implied by integrability (would need a C² conjugacy of T on a leaf to a rotation), so their hypothesis is stronger than the conjecture's. c07 also imposes global continuity of the leaf function on all of ℝ².
